notes.title: Patch: Error handling
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/b85ce18cc582d8cc2b822e66416112bfe19aa16a.png

This patch adds better error handling in the event that a failure happens during saving or loading of important game data.

These errors can happen due to a variety of causes, the most extreme would be system failure during read/write operations, with the most minor being caused by exiting the game while saving/loading, or blocking saving/loading by having a file open while the game is trying to access it. 

If you happen to have an issue, the game will start in a safe mode and provide some instructions on how to try to fix the error.

I've made a significant effort to wrap all read/write operations with safety checks, and provided an error log to help debug the problem. If you cannot get back up and running, please reach out and I will do my best to help you.

If there is an error log, a timestamped file will be placed in the directory: [YOUR_WINDOWS_USER_PATH]/AppData/LocalLow/ScopatGames/vrkshop/ErrorLogs/

Have fun. Be productive.

notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/093aaf22ec27a28074da054886dde6e5ce7121c4.png

This small update brings performance enhancements and gameplay bug fixes that I have been meaning to buckle down and sort out for a long time. 

Gameplay fixes: 

- Fixed bug with sawing multiple lumber. The saw now behaves more consistently when sawing through multiple lumber within the same lumber assembly and when sawing stacks of loose lumber.

- Large lumber assemblies no longer jump/hop when new lumber is nailed or when a member lumber is sawed

- Fixed mass calculation bug for certain orientations when sawing on a lumber assembly. This caused assemblies to lose their mass and seem very squishy. This no longer happens.

- Added consideration to the center of mass when computing the stiffness and damping properties of hand grips. This makes large, lightweight items not be as springy while holding them. (e.g. 5 boards strung together in a single line).

- Fixed a bug with the table vise so it grabs items more reliably on the first try.

- Fixed bug with manipulating lumber assemblies while they are held in the table vise, and then the table vise releasing the assemblies. This no longer happens.


Increased performance: 

- Changed from multi pass to single pass stereo rendering

- Using more shared materials to reduce draw calls

- Combined static meshes on main menu scene

- Ensured small meshes using same materials are being dynamically batched (e.g. primarily nails and lumber)

- Added Level of Detail to nails. They render more simplified or get culled as they are further away from you to save rendering time.

-----------------------------------

Check it out and be sure to leave comments in the Discord server or Steam Community Forums.

Have fun. Be productive.

notes.title: Update 5: Getting Physical (and more)
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/a099ba663182e2300b4e75cec3505b97072b60de.png

The purpose of this update was to address a lot of the physics related issues that I've received feedback on over the initial weeks of vrkshop being available on Early Access. I've tried my best to take in, digest, and offer an incremental step towards more stable and predictable interactions, without giving up too much of the physical world.

As always, tell me what is working for you or what needs more attention. Thank you to those who have provided detailed descriptions of issues!

What is in the update?

More present physical 'hands'

The 'hands' no longer pass through the static objects in the room. Previously, your hand indicators tracked with your controllers fairly reliably. This caused a lot of problems with giving your hands god-like strength. 

A major benefit to this new behavior is that you can no longer punch your hands into the wall, and then grab the saw, causing it to jump into the netherworld between the vrkshop and the horrors of the outer-vrkshop. This is a mechanism I overlooked, well, simply because I developed the game and didn't realize people would do that.

-grab lock- replaces -pickup- action

The -pickup- action has been replaced with -grab lock-. Aside from sounding more specific, the -grab lock- action works different from the plain -grab- when used on the SAW and the HAMMER. 

Using the plain -grab- action will grab the saw or hammer in the orientation that it is lying in, and not flip the tool around to the preset grab orientation.

-grab lock- will snap the SAW or HAMMER to the predefined grab orientation for those tools. Of course, -grab lock- still allows you to lock any other item to your grip like before.

This give you a little more flexibility with holding these tools, and hopefully further prevents the rage inducing scattering of your project across the room when all you were trying to do was move the hammer.

Other various changes:

[olist] Added dynamic physics joint parameters based on an object's mass. This addresses the overly droopy and swingy heavy object grab behavior.

 Hands can now interact with the clipboard and calculator, no longer requiring the use of a pencil

 Modified workbench colliders to attempt to fix the ghost sliding of lumber

 Reduced the player grab distance to 0.15m to reduce inadvertent grabbing of stuff.

 Fixed a bug with respect to the grabbing of a nail or pill causing the loss of grab functionality of the hand.

 Added a 'no hand' icon warning instead of the 'x' when the player tries to saw a board while holding it, or tries to interrupt a sawing action by grabbing the item

 When a nail box is empty, it can now be discarded, or will be discarded on the next loading of a saved game, tidying up your vrkshop

 Added some margin on the smooth locomotion so the player no longer "plummets into the dirt through a 2mm gap in my 2x6 scaffolding"

 Added a player and item respawn feature if the player or items go outside of the play area.

 Added snacks to the free play material order form for Twash
[/olist]

And I'm sure I've added a few bugs in there along the way, so be sure to report those in the Community Forums.

Have fun. Be productive.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/d623ca37bd0fc99380da82d13b0994be02b0e626.png

Smooth locomotion is now an option that can be toggled on the clipboard options. Movement and rotation options can be toggled separately.

There are two types of smooth movement:

LOOK DIRECTION: Hold both the left-hand and right-hand teleport buttons down to move in the direction you are looking.

FREE MOVEMENT (Twin stick): Use the left joystick for forward/back & side strafing, and the right joystick for smooth rotation.

Note for Vive users: 
Vive controllers only have the first option (look movement) available in the default SteamVR controller bindings. You can manually override by providing a binding to the 'move' and 'rotate' actions. These will work on the touchpads, but are incredibly sensitive.

Update 2: A Grabbing and Physics Update
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/cafbdded927aabbcfd7421b26be1cee85ac53b7e.png

In this update I've started to address some of the issues around grabbing items and the physics joints and inter-item interaction.

Here is a list of things addressed:

1. The fixed-hold orientation items (the saw and hammer most noticeably) no longer snap to their rotation, but instead attempt to smoothly interpolate to the final rotation. You should notice a lot fewer items flying around your vrkshop (at least unintended items flying around your vrkshop).

2. You can now transfer items from one hand to the other with both -grab- and -pickup- (hold-lock) actions. This makes it easier to inspect items without dropping and re-picking them up. 

Note: While I'm on this topic, this is a reminder that if an item is 'stuck' to your hand, try pressing the -pickup- action button to release it.

3. I more than doubled the distance that your real-world hand can move away from the in-game saw while sawing, before it cancels the sawing action. 

Note, I am still working on a fix for the saw failing on a high percentage of cuts.

4. I increased the angle for the hammer to detect a nail head for removal. It should be easier to attach now.

5. I added a cooldown timer for haptics on items to prevent the "run-away" haptics response due to some collision situations.

6. I added a linear displacement, instead of purely a rotational displacement, to the joint of handheld items. You will notice a change to the general dynamics of items in your hand, but the major benefit is that it is harder to push items through objects.

I hope you find these updates helpful, and as always, leave feedback in the Steam Community Forums.

Have fun. Be productive.

- wooden robot

notes.title: Small Patch Update 1.1
notes.notes:
Small Patch Update 1.1: Pencil, Straightedge, Chalk Fixes

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/d52485d8d984d330c569af53769b770ec32fded3.png

Today I pushed a small patch update fixing the following!

1. I darkened the pencil lines so they are now more visible in the shadows. 
2. The pencil now works more smoothly, both in 'interact' mode and 'touch' mode.
3. The pencil now transitions smoothly to a nearby straightedge tool (speed square, or framing squares)
4. The chalk now attaches and releases from the chalkboard a bit smoother.
5. The chalkboard should be slightly faster now.

Have fun. Be productive.

- wooden robot

notes.title: vrkshop Update 1: Dimensions on chalkboard
notes.notes:
Dimensions on the chalkboard are here to the rescue!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38017136/12fb5cda65f3af95d986a394bda8493c4ad81ada.jpg

A new 'hints' tab appeared on the clipboard. This allows you to enable hints for the project you are currently working on. Hints mostly include dimensions, but they may also include a few other surprises.

Minor Teleport Adjustment

In this update, I also adjusted the teleport beam angle to hopefully alleviate some of the discomfort of wrenching your wrists around to point at the floor.

Feedback is very welcome on the Steam Community forum.

Have fun. Be productive.

- wooden robot
